provenanceNote: Rebased onto main 99a7d0c (#227, the post-dive screen), which on the first completed state clears the save and, in a microtask, tears the dive down and shows the post-dive screen. Conflicts: src/app/wreck-app.ts keeps #227's single `ended` flag with its teardown and routing, with this slice's thirdsTurnWarned latch beside it; the completed-dive audio stop this slice's base had in onFrame is #227's teardown now. docs/baseline/claims-register.json keeps #227's post-dive anchors under SAFETY-STOP-001, DECOMPRESSION-001, GAS-001 and ASCENT-001 with this slice's HUD anchors added after them. 71144f6 adapts the browser test of a dive surfaced fast past its stop to the post-dive routing: it asserts the post-dive screen and that no HUD, warning or chip stays; the presentation's no-rate, no-stop rule for a completed dive stays pinned in the unit test. The freshness logic and everything else Codex reviewed are unchanged. On main ce8b666, the squash of slice 7a (#223). After 811fc86, 7a gained a silent completed dive, the torch and the nav pad only while diving, the waves stopped after the end, and the 18 m BCD fixture compared to 12 places. The rebase onto ce8b666 (git rebase --onto origin/main 811fc86) kept this slice's own commits and applied without conflicts: updateHud keeps 7a's hiding of the nav pad and torch beside this slice's readouts, and the claims register keeps main's anchors beside this slice's. 17cecdf compares the 28 m neutral BCD fixture to 12 places, as Math.pow differs in the last bits on linux CI. 0c4e812 reads a completed dive's ascent rate as 0 and shows it no safety stop: a completed dive is never stepped again, so a dive surfaced fast past a paused stop kept the SLOW DOWN warning, '⚠ ↑ 25 m/min' and the paused stop row on its HUD for good, where legacy's post-dive state draws no dive computer. f1a7b30 addresses pre-review pass 1 on #226: the stop row keeps legacy's 'SAFETY STOP / Complete' once done, until the stop starts over below 11 m or the dive ends, and gives way to deco on the model's ceiling of the same tick (log.lastCeilingM at the dive's GF high, legacy's frameCalc.ceiling) instead of the worker's forecast, which is pending after every gas switch, setpoint change and bailout and on a resumed dive. 9119385 and 9fc2322 close two first-frame races in existing specs: the CNS test lost an I press on linux CI (run for 722438f), and the cross-client trace failed once on 9119385 under load (below); both now wait for the dive's first frame, with no assertion changed. The surface wait reads 0 m/min with no stop and no gauge, as legacy's drawSurface() draws the dive computer at rest. e020fe1 addresses Codex round 1 on #226: under a ceiling the safety stop gave way but the row hid, so no HUD path showed the decompression stop. The row is now legacy's whole stop box: while the model's ceiling of the tick is above 0 it reads 'Deco stop' in the danger tone with the forecast's first stop (legacy's frameCalc.schedule.stops[0], minutes rounded up), and the title alone while no forecast with stops is in hand, as legacy's box without a schedule. eef09ab addresses Codex round 2 on #226: the deco row took its numbers from whatever forecast was cached, and a dropped worker answer under fast-forward left them for the client's 5 s timeout (150 dive seconds at x30). The controller keeps, with each accepted forecast, the dive time and depth of the state it was requested for and the clock rate it was requested at; the numbers show only while the forecast is current, else the title alone: its age at most the scheduler's 2 s interval plus 0.5 s of real time at the faster of the requested and current clock rates (3.5 dive s at x3, 17 at x30), and its depth within 1.5 m (the scheduler re-asks on each whole metre). d55f5c2 adds the exact stop check: the forecast's first stop must equal decoStopDepth(lastCeilingM), the same ceilingDepthM at the same GF high and the same rounding as the planner's first stop (src/planner/dive-planner.ts 175; legacy src/physics.js 350-366), so a forecast naming 6 m while the model's ceiling names 3 m shows the title alone even within the time budget; and the scheduler asks again on the frame the model's stop moves, so the title stands alone at a stop boundary only until that answer lands (4 frames in the test, 36 without it at x3). 89688f1 addresses pre-review pass 5: the dive-time budget takes the faster of the requested and current rates, so a forecast asked at x30 kept 17 dive seconds, 5.7 s of real time, once fast-forward ended. The controller now records its real time with the source, and a forecast is current only while the real time since its request is at most the interval at the rate it was asked at plus 0.5 s (1.17 s at x3, 0.57 s at x30), beside the unchanged dive-time and depth bounds; the budget's comment now derives it with the next request waiting for the previous answer. 63e57b4 adds the test in which the dive-time bound alone binds (asked at x3, fast-forward then on). 412d79a addresses pre-review pass 6: the real-time bound now takes the interval at the slower of the requested and current rates, because once fast-forward ends the next request is due only after the interval at x3 (0.67 s real), and a x30 forecast's 0.57 s ran out first, blanking the numbers for about 130 ms with a prompt worker; it is 0.57 s while fast-forwarding throughout and 1.17 s once either rate is x3. The full run above is on 71144f6; later commits only update this file, so src, tests, scripts and docs are identical to the measured tree (see durableProvenance).

portedFromTheOracle.ascentRate: src/renderer.js drawDiveComputer: the chevrons' direction past 0.5 m/min and Math.round(|ascentRate|) in m/min; the rate is the model's log.ascentRateMpm, legacy's -(depth - prevDepth) / dtDiveMinutes.
portedFromTheOracle.fastAscent: The warning banner's SLOW DOWN past 9 m/min up (warnSlow), ranked below the oxygen warning and above the gas warnings as legacy's banner ranks it, with the hasWarning beep through the alert.warning cue; in words in the alert region and the status chip, and a ⚠ on the rate's row.
portedFromTheOracle.safetyStop: The stop box's safety-stop half: the nominal depth round((2.4 + 8.3) / 2) = 5 m with calculateSafetyStopDuration() before the countdown, then the floored countdown, paused (caution tone, and the word) outside the band; once done, `else if (safetyStopComplete)`: 'SAFETY STOP / Complete', until the diver goes back below 11 m (the model's reset) or the dive ends. Legacy draws the English literal in both languages; the German row reads 'Absolviert', legacy's German debrief word (gradeNotes.safetyDone). While there is a ceiling the box shows the decompression stop instead (showStopBox = inDeco || ...): decided on the model's log.lastCeilingM, legacy's frameCalc.ceiling of the same tick, not on the worker's forecast.
portedFromTheOracle.ruleOfThirds: hud-thirds: shown under an overhead, the phase by legacy's strict > 2/3 and > 1/3 over all cylinders' gas against the plan, and Math.round of the fraction; the turn in the caution tone, the reserve with the ⚠ of its danger tone; playAlertBeep() once as thirdsTurnWarned latches, not again on resuming a latched dive.
portedFromTheOracle.claims: docs/baseline/claims-register.json anchors the new strings in both locales: wreck.warning.fastAscent, wreck.hud.warning.fastAscent and wreck.hud.ascentRate* under ASCENT-001, wreck.hud.safetyStop* (Complete included) under SAFETY-STOP-001, wreck.hud.decoStop* under DECOMPRESSION-001, wreck.hud.thirds* under GAS-001.
portedFromTheOracle.afterTheEnd: Legacy's post-dive state draws no dive computer, and updateCompletion logs a stop not made as skipped as the dive ends: the presentation reads a completed dive's rate as 0 and owes it no stop, so the rate row, the SLOW DOWN warning and the stop row do not stay frozen on the ended dive's HUD.
portedFromTheOracle.decoStop: The stop box's decompression half, `if (inDeco)` with inDeco = decoStop(frameCalc.ceiling) > 0: shown while the model's log.lastCeilingM, legacy's frameCalc.ceiling of the same tick at the dive's GF high, is above 0; the DECO STOP title in the danger tone, here 'Deco stop' / 'Dekompressionsstopp' (legacy's English literal, in the catalogue's decompression wording); with `schedule && schedule.stops.length > 0`, the first stop's depth in m and its minutes, from the forecast's schedule (frameCalc.schedule, which the worker computes here; the planner rounds the minutes up as calculateDecoSchedule's Math.ceil). With no schedule, the title alone. No banner or beep is added: legacy's deco warning, ABOVE CEILING — DESCEND when the diver is shallower than the stop, is not in the migration's warnings yet (#228). Legacy reads frameCalc.schedule of the same frame; the worker's forecast is asynchronous, so its numbers are shown only while it still describes the dive (isForecastCurrent): computed from a state at most the scheduler's interval plus 0.5 s real (at the faster of the requested and current clock rates) earlier in dive time, requested at most the interval at the slower of its rate and the current rate plus 0.5 s ago in real time, and within 1.5 m of the diver's depth. The schedule's first stop is decoStop() of the ceiling at GF high, in legacy (src/physics.js calculateDecoSchedule, firstStop = decoStop(frameCalc.ceiling)) and in the planner (calculateDecoSchedule, decoStopDepth(calculateCeiling) at gfHighPercent); GF low only shapes the stops' lengths. The numbers also require the forecast's first stop to equal decoStopDepth(lastCeilingM), exact by construction, and the forecast scheduler includes that stop in its input signature so a boundary crossing is re-forecast at once.
